speaker: Doctor
text: I'm sorry to hear you're experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any muscle twitching or drooping of your eyelids recently?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that clarification; the pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest is very telling. Given your age group (if young) or specific triggers, have you experienced any episodes of drooping eyelids or slurred speech in the past? Also, do you have a personal or family history of autoimmune diseases?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the symmetrical weakness and lack of family history. Given the classic pattern of fatigue-related weakness and eye symptoms, have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or breathing, especially when lying down? REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR Antibodies. speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Anti-AChR Antibodies: Present (elevated); EMG_Nerve_Conduction: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss. You must output exactly the following diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS READY: Tuberculosis

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.

This diagnosis is based on your symptoms of fluctuating muscle weakness that worsens with activity and improves with rest, combined with double vision. The requested Anti-AChR Antibody test and EMG will confirm this, and we should proceed with treatment planning immediately.
